Troubleshooting

2026-11-11

Source: vignettes/troubleshooting.Rmd
troubleshooting.Rmd

Build synapser

When you build synapser from source locally, you need to install reticulate and rjson first. Otherwise, you will run into the following error:

$ R CMD BUILD .

* installing to library ‘/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.5-arm64/Resources/library’
ERROR: dependency ‘reticulate’ is not available for package ‘synapser’
Perhaps try a variation of:
install.packages('reticulate')
* removing ‘/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.5-arm64/Resources/library/synapser’

Dependency Conflicts (rjson/reticulate)

synapser 3.0.0 works with current versions of rjson and reticulate, so the version conflicts reported against synapser 2.x no longer apply. This issue will be automatically resolved if you install synapser from R-Universe. However, if you build synapser from source locally, and you have older versions of rjson and reticulate installed, you will see an error like:

$ R CMD BUILD .

* installing to library ‘/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.5-arm64/Resources/library’
* installing *source* package ‘synapser’ ...
** this is package ‘synapser’ version ‘3.0.0’
** using staged installation
Error: 'py_require' is not an exported object from 'namespace:reticulate'
Execution halted
ERROR: configuration failed for package ‘synapser’
* removing ‘/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.5-arm64/Resources/library/synapser’

In this case, you should upgrade these packages first before installing synapser.

install.packages(c("rjson", "reticulate"))

Python Version Compatibility

You do not need to install Python for synapser 3.0.0. On first use, reticulate downloads a compatible Python and the Synapse Python client into a managed environment.

Load synapser first and check which Python synapser is using:

reticulate::py_config()

lexical error: invalid char in json text on Windows

Loading synapser fails with:

Error : lexical error: invalid char in json text.
                                       warning: Failed to inspect Pyth
                     (right here) ------^
...
error: Suitable Python installation for creating a venv not found.

Windows has a registry entry for a Python installation whose files no longer exist, for example because its folder was deleted by hand or its uninstall did not finish. uv warns that it cannot inspect that Python, and reticulate fails to read uv’s output, so it never downloads a managed Python.

To see which Python is causing it, run:

system2(reticulate:::uv_binary(), c("python", "list", "--output-format", "json"))

The first line of output names the missing interpreter, e.g.:

warning: Failed to inspect Python interpreter from registry at `C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python314\python.exe`

To fix it, do one of the following, then restart R and load synapser again:

  • Delete the stale registry key from Command Prompt, using the version from the warning. List the registered versions first:

    reg query HKCU\Software\Python\PythonCore
reg delete HKCU\Software\Python\PythonCore\3.14 /f

    If the missing Python was installed for all users (under C:\Program Files), use HKLM instead of HKCU, from a Command Prompt run as administrator.

  • Reinstall that Python version from python.org. You can keep it, or uninstall it through Settings > Apps, which removes the registry entry properly.

synapser only runs in the Python environment reticulate manages with uv, but Python was already initialized in this R session

Loading synapser fails with:

Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘synapser’:
 .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'synapser', details:
  call: NULL
  error: synapser only runs in the Python environment reticulate manages with uv, but Python was already initialized in this R session with:
  <path to python>
Restart R and load synapser before anything else that uses Python.

To fix it, restart your R session and load synapser before any other packages that use Python.

R Version Compatibility

Important: synapser 3.0.0 requires R 4.2.0 or later.

R 4.1.x is not supported. It is the last Windows release with 32-bit (i386) multiarch, and reticulate 1.44.0 or later — which synapser requires in order to work with uv 0.8.0 and later — does not compile for 32-bit Windows.

Troubleshooting R Version Issues

Check your R version:

R.version.string

If installation selects an older synapser than you expect: - Verify your R version is 4.2.0 or later - Verify your reticulate version is 1.44.0 or later: packageVersion("reticulate") - Consider using the recommended installation method with version specification

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian):

# Remove current R version
sudo apt remove r-base r-base-core r-base-dev

# Add CRAN repository for specific R version
sudo apt update
sudo apt install software-properties-common
sudo add-apt-repository "deb https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu $(lsb_release -cs)-cran40/"

# Install R 4.4
sudo apt install r-base=4.4.2-1cran1.2004.0 r-base-core=4.4.2-1cran1.2004.0

Linux (Amazon Linux/RHEL/CentOS):

# Remove current R version
sudo dnf remove R R-core R-devel

# Install from source (recommended for version control)
sudo dnf groupinstall -y "Development Tools"
sudo dnf install -y gcc-gfortran readline-devel libX11-devel libXt-devel \
    zlib-devel bzip2-devel xz-devel pcre2-devel curl-devel

# Download and compile R 4.4.2
cd /tmp
wget https://cran.r-project.org/src/base/R-4/R-4.4.2.tar.gz
tar -xzf R-4.4.2.tar.gz
cd R-4.4.2
./configure --enable-R-shlib --with-blas --with-lapack
make
sudo make install

# Fix PATH if older R version is still being used
echo 'export PATH="/usr/local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc

Verify Installation:

R.version.string

Troubleshooting Amazon Linux R Installation: If which R still shows an old R version after compilation:

# Check current R location
which R

# If it shows /usr/local/R-4.5.1/bin/R instead of /usr/local/bin/R:
export PATH="/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
echo 'export PATH="/usr/local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc

Type Conversions

The core of the synapser library is the python client. Reticulate is used to translate R to Python and back.

These are the documented conversions from R to Python: Reticulate Type Conversions

NA has no direct equivalent in Python. synapser does not rewrite NA to None (or to NULL); it passes values through reticulate, which converts NA according to the type of the vector rather than mapping it to None.

When working with R and Reticulate, NA values in types tables are converted by Reticulate depending on the data type.

For numeric data types, NA values are converted to the corresponding R value NA_real_. For integer data types, NA values are converted to NA_integer_. For logical data types, NA values are converted to NA_logical_. For character data types, NA values are converted to NA_character_.

In addition, Reticulate also converts any values that cannot be coerced to the specified data type to NA_character_.

Reticulate performs these conversions automatically.

When Reticulate converts R objects to Python, NA is not mapped to None. None is what reticulate uses for R NULL. Conversion of NA depends on type, and the missing value is not always preserved: logical NA becomes Python True and comes back as TRUE; character NA becomes the Python string "NA" and comes back as "NA"; integer NA becomes -2147483648 and comes back as NA, numeric NA becomes nan and comes back as NA.

Example:

na_values <- list(
  logical = c(TRUE, FALSE, NA),
  character = c("T", "F", NA),
  integer = c(1L, 2L, NA),
  numeric = c(1538006762583, 1538006762584, NA)
)
na_py <- reticulate::r_to_py(na_values)
na_py
## {'logical': [True, False, True], 'character': ['T', 'F', 'NA'], 'integer': [1, 2, -2147483648], 'numeric': [1538006762583.0, 1538006762584.0, nan]}
na_r <- reticulate::py_to_r(na_py)
na_r
## $logical
## [1]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE
## 
## $character
## [1] "T"  "F"  "NA"
## 
## $integer
## [1]  1  2 NA
## 
## $numeric
## [1] 1.538007e+12 1.538007e+12           NA

Poisoned cache and endswith error

Starting with the Synapse Python client version 4.2.0, a change to how the Synapse Cache writes entries was introduced. The purpose of the change was to more accurately track when a file was last modified, and what the MD5 checksum of the file was at that point in time. Prior to this change the Synapse cache was a simple key-value store, however, with the new change, the cache is now a dictionary of dictionaries.

If you find that you receive the following error when trying to use synGet:

> synapser::synGet("syn12345")
Error in value[[3L]](cond) : 'dict' object has no attribute 'endswith'

You may have a “poisoned” cache. This can happen if you, or someone using the file system where your Synapse cache is stored, has run the newer Synapse Python client - while you are still using the older version of synapser/Python Client.

To resolve this issue, you can either:

  1. Delete the Synapse cache directory: This will force synapser to re-download all files from Synapse and rebuild the cache. By default, the cache is stored in ~/.synapseCache.

    Note: The following suggested commands have the potential to delete many files, so please ensure you have backups of any important data before running them. The cache directory is typically used to store temporary files and metadata. Deleting this data will only affect your local machine - It will not affect any data that is stored in Synapse. This will require you to re-download files from Synapse.

    The exact commands will depend on your operating system, but here are some examples:

    • Linux/macOS:

      rm -rf ~/.synapseCache

    • Windows:

      Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $HOME\.synapseCache

  2. Upgrade to the latest version of synapser: This will ensure that you are using the latest version of the Synapse Python client, which is compatible with the new cache format.

install.packages(
  "synapser",
  repos = c("https://sage-bionetworks.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org")
)
